statute_name: Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 (SARFAESI Act)

regulatory_authority.title: Master Circular - Prudential norms on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning pertaining to Advances (IRAC Framework)

13(2).description: Demand Notice by Secured Creditor calling upon borrower to clear liabilities within 60 days.

13(3A).description: Mandatory requirement for Secured Creditor to consider Borrower's representation/objection and communicate reasoned response within 15 days if rejected.

13(4).description: Recourse to measures (taking possession, management of asset, appointing manager) upon non-payment after 60 days.

14.description: Application to Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) / District Magistrate (DM) for physical possession assistance.

17.description: Application against measures (Securitisation Application / SA) before Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT) within 45 days of measure.

18.description: Appeal to Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal (DRAT) within 30 days of DRT order with mandatory pre-deposit (50% reducible to 25%).

26D.description: Mandatory CERSAI Registration: Prohibition on secured creditor exercising rights under Chapter III unless security interest is registered with CERSAI.

26E.description: Priority of Secured Creditors: Priority of secured debt over all other debts, taxes, revenues, or statutory dues payable to Central/State Govt.

31(g).description: De Minimis Debt Exemption: SARFAESI Act shall NOT apply to any case where the amount due is less than ₹100,000 or less than 20% of principal & interest.

31(i).description: Exemption of Agricultural Land: Provisions of SARFAESI Act shall NOT apply to any security interest created in agricultural land.

32.description: Protection of Action Taken in Good Faith: Absolute bar on civil/criminal proceedings against Authorized Officer for actions taken under SARFAESI Act.

rules.rule_8_1: Possession Notice served on borrower and affixed at outer door of property.
rules.rule_8_2: Possession Notice must be published in 2 leading newspapers (1 in vernacular language) within 7 days.
rules.rule_8_6: Mandatory 30-day public notice to borrower prior to sale/auction of immovable property (reduced to 15 days for subsequent auctions).
rules.rule_9_1: No sale of immovable property shall take place before expiry of 30 days from newspaper publication of auction notice.

fatal_defects.name: Failure to Reply to Section 13(3A) Representation within 15 Days
fatal_defects.ratio: Mardia Chemicals Ltd. v. UOI (2004) 4 SCC 311: Non-consideration of borrower's objection or failure to communicate reasoned decision within statutory period vitiates subsequent Section 13(4) possession measures.

fatal_defects.name: Non-Registration of Security Interest with CERSAI
fatal_defects.ratio: Section 26D imposes an absolute statutory bar on secured creditors exercising enforcement rights under Chapter III unless the security interest is registered on CERSAI portal.

fatal_defects.name: Enforcement Action against Agricultural Land
fatal_defects.ratio: ITC Ltd. v. Blue Coast Hotels Ltd. (2018) 15 SCC 99 & K. Sreedhar v. R. Velusamy (2022): Security interest created over agricultural land is completely exempt from SARFAESI enforcement.

fatal_defects.name: Securitisation Application (SA) Filed Beyond 45 Days
fatal_defects.ratio: B. Arvind Kumar v. Govt. of India (2007) 5 SCC 745: S.17 SA must be filed within strict 45-day limitation period from date of S.13(4) measure. Limitation cannot be condoned without sufficient cause.

fatal_defects.name: Breach of Mandatory 30-Day Auction Notice under Rule 8(6)/9(1)
fatal_defects.ratio: Mathew Varghese v. M. Amritha Kumar (2014) 5 SCC 610: 30-day notice to borrower under Rule 8(6) and publication under Rule 9(1) are mandatory. Any sale conducted in violation thereof is void ab initio.

precedents.citation: Mardia Chemicals Ltd. v. Union of India (2004) 4 SCC 311
precedents.proposition_supported: Reasoned reply to Section 13(3A) representation is mandatory before taking Section 13(4) measures.
principles: Constitutional validity of SARFAESI Act upheld.
Requirement of 75% pre-deposit under Section 17 struck down as unconstitutional (subsequently amended to 50%/25% under Section 18).
Reasoned reply to Section 13(3A) representation is mandatory before taking Section 13(4) measures.

precedents.citation: Transcore v. Union of India (2008) 1 SCC 125
precedents.proposition_supported: Secured creditor is not required to withdraw DRT suit before taking recourse to SARFAESI Act.
principles: Secured creditor is not required to withdraw DRT suit under OA 1993 before taking recourse to SARFAESI Act.
SARFAESI Act is an additional cumulative remedy for banks.

precedents.citation: United Bank of India v. Satyawati Tondon (2010) 8 SCC 110
precedents.proposition_supported: High Courts must not entertain Article 226 Writ Petitions against SARFAESI actions when statutory remedy under Section 17 DRT is available.
principles: High Courts must not entertain Article 226 Writ Petitions against SARFAESI actions when effective statutory remedy under Section 17 DRT is available.

precedents.citation: Standard Chartered Bank v. V. Noble Kumar (2013) 9 SCC 620
precedents.proposition_supported: Secured creditor can approach DM/CMM under Section 14 directly without first taking physical resistance under Section 13(4).
principles: Bank can directly apply under Section 14 to DM/CMM without taking symbolic possession under Section 13(4) first.
Section 14 provides an independent mechanism for physical possession assistance.

precedents.citation: Mathew Varghese v. M. Amritha Kumar (2014) 5 SCC 610
precedents.proposition_supported: Compliance with Rule 8(6) and Rule 9(1) is mandatory to protect borrower's right of redemption under Section 13(8).
principles: Compliance with Rule 8(6) and Rule 9(1) is mandatory to protect borrower's right of redemption under Section 13(8).

precedents.citation: ITC Ltd. v. Blue Coast Hotels Ltd. (2018) 15 SCC 99
precedents.proposition_supported: Agricultural land exemption under Section 31(i) applies based on revenue records at the time of security creation.
principles: Debtor's proposal for settlement under Section 13(3A) does not constitute waiver of statutory protections.
Agricultural land classification U/S 31(i) must be established based on actual land use and revenue records.

precedents.citation: Bajarang Shyamsunder Agarwal v. Central Bank of India (2019) 9 SCC 94
precedents.proposition_supported: Tenants claiming under valid lease created prior to mortgage cannot be dispossessed under Section 14 without due process of law.
principles: Valid tenancy created prior to mortgage is protected against summary Section 14 dispossession.
CMM/DM must examine bona fides of tenancy claims before executing physical possession orders.

precedents.citation: K. Virupaksha v. State of Karnataka (2020) 4 SCC 440
precedents.proposition_supported: Absolute protection against criminal prosecution granted to Bank Officers under Section 32 for actions in good faith.
principles: Section 32 of SARFAESI Act bars criminal proceedings against Authorized Officers acting in good faith under the Act.
Borrowers cannot bypass Section 17 DRT remedy by lodging criminal FIRs against bank officials.

precedents.citation: Indian Overseas Bank v. RCM Infrastructure Ltd. (2022) SCC OnLine SC 634
precedents.proposition_supported: NCLT CIRP Moratorium declared under Section 14 IBC stays all SARFAESI enforcement & auction sales.
principles: Section 14 Moratorium under IBC overrides SARFAESI enforcement once CIRP is admitted by NCLT.
Sale completed or balance payment received during Moratorium period is null and void.

precedents.citation: Celir LLP v. Bafna Motors (Mumbai) Pvt. Ltd. (2023) SCC OnLine SC 1209
precedents.proposition_supported: Borrower's right of redemption under Section 13(8) stands extinguished on publication of auction notice.
principles: Borrower's right of redemption under Section 13(8) stands extinguished on the date of publication of auction notice, not on auction completion date.
